📏 Language models

Context window

In simple words

The amount of text, measured in tokens, that a language model can take into account at once.

The longest stretch of text, counted in tokens, that a language model can look at at one time: your messages, its own answers and any documents you give it. Whatever doesn't fit is invisible to it, which is why a very long chat can “forget” its beginning.

Example. It's like reading a long story through a window that shows only the last few pages. By 2025, some models' windows held hundreds of thousands of tokens — as much as a whole novel, or more.

Lessons that teach it

  • Lesson 9: How Chatbots Write

Related words

  • TokenA small piece of text, such as a word or part of a word, that a language model reads and writes.
  • AttentionThe part of a transformer that lets each word look at the other words and decide which of them matter for its meaning.
  • PromptThe instruction or question you give to a generative AI.
